$schema.description: Centralized catalogue for the Neurodivergence Library. Every entry must be a real, verifiable publication: check the DOI resolves before adding it. Entries link out to the publisher rather than redistributing PDFs we have no licence to host. To add a resource, append one object to the `resources` array. If you hold the rights to a document, you may additionally drop the file into /public/downloads and set `downloadUrl`.

fields.title: string — the publication's exact title
fields.description: string — plain-language summary of what the work actually found
fields.category: string — MUST match one of the values in `categories` exactly
fields.type: string — one of: Journal Article | Review | Meta-Analysis | Consensus Statement
fields.authorOrInstitution: string — the real authors, as published
fields.publishDate: string — 'YYYY' or 'YYYY-MM-DD'; use year-only when the month is not certain
fields.sourceUrl: string — canonical DOI link; must resolve
fields.openAccessUrl: string (optional) — free full text (repository, PMC, publisher OA)
fields.abstract: string (optional) — accurate summary shown in the 'Read Abstract' panel
fields.featured: boolean (optional) — surfaces the entry in 'Cutting-Edge Research'
fields.downloadUrl: string (optional) — ONLY for documents you have the right to host, e.g. /downloads/my-file.pdf

resources.title: On the ontological status of autism: the 'double empathy problem'
resources.description: The paper that introduced the double empathy problem: the argument that breakdowns between autistic and non-autistic people are mutual, not a one-sided deficit in autistic understanding.
resources.abstract: Milton challenges the framing of autism through cognitive-deficit models, arguing that when people of very different experience interact, the failure of mutual understanding is shared. Non-autistic people are no better at reading autistic minds than the reverse — so the 'empathy problem' is double, and located between people rather than inside one of them.

resources.title: Autistic peer-to-peer information transfer is highly effective
resources.description: Empirical support for the double empathy problem: information passed along chains of autistic people was retained as well as in non-autistic chains, while mixed chains lost significantly more detail.
resources.authorOrInstitution: Catherine J. Crompton, Danielle Ropar, Claire V. M. Evans-Williams, Emma G. Flynn & Sue Fletcher-Watson
resources.abstract: Using diffusion chains of eight participants (n = 72), a story was passed from person to person in all-autistic, all-non-autistic and mixed chains. Detail retention declined significantly more steeply in the mixed chains, while autistic chains did not differ significantly from non-autistic ones — evidence that autistic people transfer information effectively to each other, and that difficulty arises across neurotypes rather than within autism.

resources.title: Attention, monotropism and the diagnostic criteria for autism
resources.description: The foundational monotropism paper, arguing that atypical allocation of attention — deep interest in fewer things at once — is central to the autistic experience.
resources.authorOrInstitution: Dinah Murray, Mike Lesser & Wenn Lawson
resources.abstract: Drawing on a range of literature, the authors argue that atypical strategies for allocating attention are central to autism. The account is examined against the DSM-IV and ICD-10 diagnostic criteria and against the personal experience of autistic people, including one of the authors.

resources.title: "Having All of Your Internal Resources Exhausted Beyond Measure and Being Left with No Clean-Up Crew": Defining Autistic Burnout
resources.description: The first community-based study to define autistic burnout, characterising it as chronic exhaustion, loss of skills and reduced tolerance to stimuli — distinct from depression.
resources.authorOrInstitution: Dora M. Raymaker, Alan R. Teo, Nicole A. Steckler, Brandy Lentz, Mirah Scharer, Austin Delos Santos, Steven K. Kapp, Morrigan Hunter, Andee Joyce & Christina Nicolaidis
resources.abstract: Using a community-based participatory research approach, the authors thematically analysed 19 interviews and 19 public internet sources to characterise autistic burnout as chronic exhaustion, loss of skills and reduced tolerance to stimulus, arising from life stressors and barriers to support. Participants distinguished it from depression and from occupational burnout.

resources.title: Pathological demand avoidance syndrome: a necessary distinction within the pervasive developmental disorders
resources.description: The original clinical account of demand avoidance as a distinct profile, and the starting point for the ongoing debate about how PDA should be understood and supported.
resources.authorOrInstitution: Elizabeth Newson, Kimberley Le Maréchal & Clare David
resources.abstract: Newson and colleagues describe a group of children whose central feature is extreme avoidance of everyday demands, alongside surface sociability and a need for control, and argue that this profile is clinically distinct within the pervasive developmental disorders. The classification remains contested; later work reframes the avoidance as an anxiety and autonomy response rather than deliberate non-compliance.

resources.title: The World Federation of ADHD International Consensus Statement: 208 evidence-based conclusions about the disorder
resources.description: A large international consensus statement gathering only well-replicated findings about ADHD, written explicitly to counter misinformation and stigma.
resources.authorOrInstitution: Stephen V. Faraone et al., World Federation of ADHD
resources.abstract: To counter misconceptions that stigmatise people with ADHD, the authors curated 208 conclusions supported by strong evidence — restricting inclusion to studies of more than 2,000 participants or meta-analyses of five or more studies. The result is a reference on the nature, course, outcomes, causes and treatment of ADHD.

resources.title: The neurobiology of interoception in health and disease
resources.description: A review of interoception — the sensing of the body's internal state — and how differences in it relate to autism, anxiety, depression and eating disorders.
resources.authorOrInstitution: Lisa Quadt, Hugo D. Critchley & Sarah N. Garfinkel
resources.publication: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, 1428, 112–128
resources.abstract: The authors give a neurobiological overview of interoception and set out how interoceptive differences relate to specific physical and mental health conditions, including sickness behaviour and fatigue, depression, eating disorders, autism and anxiety — supporting interest in interoception as a transdiagnostic target.

resources.title: An operational definition of twice-exceptional learners: implications and applications
resources.description: The widely-cited operational definition of 2e learners, explaining how giftedness and disability mask one another and why these students are routinely under-identified.
resources.authorOrInstitution: Sally M. Reis, Susan M. Baum & Edith Burke
resources.abstract: The authors provide a research-based rationale for an operational definition of twice-exceptionality, profile 2e youth, and summarise programmes and practices that let these students develop their strengths while their disabilities are simultaneously accommodated.

supplements.name: Omega-3 (EPA/DHA)
supplements.summary: A meta-analysis of randomised trials in children found omega-3 supplementation produced a small but statistically significant improvement in ADHD symptoms, with efficacy correlated to the EPA dose in the supplement. The effect is modest and considerably smaller than that of established treatments.
supplements.considerations: Not a replacement for standard treatment. Effects build over weeks, and omega-3 can interact with blood-thinning medication — discuss with a clinician first.
supplements.evidenceCitation: Bloch & Qawasmi (2011), Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, 50(10), 991–1000

supplements.name: Iron & Ferritin
supplements.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis found serum ferritin levels are lower on average in people with ADHD. This is an association from observational data — it does not show that supplementing iron improves symptoms in people whose levels are already normal.
supplements.considerations: Test ferritin first. Iron is harmful in excess and must never be supplemented blind, especially in children — this one is always clinician-guided.
supplements.evidenceCitation: Wang, Huang, Zhang, Qu & Mu (2017), PLOS ONE, 12(1), e0169145

supplements.name: Zinc
supplements.summary: A dose-response meta-analysis of six randomised trials in school-aged children found an effect of zinc supplementation on total ADHD scores, but not on hyperactivity or inattention subscales considered separately. The authors rated the certainty of the evidence as moderate to very low.
supplements.considerations: Weak and inconsistent evidence. Sustained high doses interfere with copper absorption, so this is worth testing for and discussing with a clinician rather than self-prescribing.
supplements.evidenceCitation: Systematic review & dose-response meta-analysis (2022), Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition, 62(32)

diagnostics.summary: Quantitative EEG analyses patterns such as the theta/beta ratio (TBR), long proposed as an objective marker for ADHD. A meta-analysis of nine studies covering 1,253 children and adolescents with ADHD found the effect size has declined substantially over time.
diagnostics.promise: Inexpensive, non-invasive and quick to administer compared with imaging.
diagnostics.caveat: The meta-analysis concluded TBR is not a reliable diagnostic measure: heterogeneity was significant and pooled effect sizes were judged an overestimate. It cannot identify individuals.
diagnostics.evidenceCitation: Arns, Conners & Kraemer (2013), Journal of Attention Disorders, 17(5), 374–383

diagnostics.method: Captures gaze patterns and visual attention
diagnostics.summary: A longitudinal infant study found that attention to others' eyes was present at birth in children later diagnosed as autistic, but declined from around two months of age — a difference measurable long before behavioural diagnosis is possible.
diagnostics.promise: Points toward far earlier identification, potentially before speech develops.
diagnostics.caveat: A group-level developmental finding from a research cohort, not a validated diagnostic test; gaze varies widely between individuals.

diagnostics.method: Maps brain anatomy, activity and connectivity
diagnostics.summary: A review of neuroimaging across the lifespan describes differences in brain structure, function and connectivity associated with autism, while setting out why these have not translated into a clinical test.
diagnostics.promise: A window into brain development that may eventually inform subtyping and more personalised support.
diagnostics.caveat: Findings are group averages with heavy overlap between individuals; no MRI measure can currently diagnose a neurodevelopmental condition.
diagnostics.evidenceCitation: Ecker, Bookheimer & Murphy (2015), The Lancet Neurology, 14(11), 1121–1134

diagnostics.summary: The first genome-wide association meta-analysis to reach significance for ADHD — 20,183 diagnosed individuals and 35,191 controls — identified variants at 12 independent loci, confirming a highly polygenic architecture of many common variants of small effect.
diagnostics.promise: Clarifies the biology of ADHD and the genetic overlap it shares with other conditions.
diagnostics.caveat: Individually these variants explain very little; polygenic scores are probabilistic, population-dependent and cannot diagnose a person.
